about.title: Personal Injury Help in Rohnert Park, California
about.longDescription: Rohnert Park's daily rhythm runs through corridors like Rohnert Park Expressway, Redwood Drive, and Golf Course Drive — routes that carry commuters, students, and shoppers across town every day. Many of these reported crashes cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when traffic is heaviest and drivers are often tired or in a hurry. If you were hurt in a collision or another type of accident here, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and lost income can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Rohnert Park with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to reach out, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out early can help preserve evidence while the details of what happened are still fresh.

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the accident — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate your claim.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, meaning your compensation isn't artificially limited to a fixed dollar amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Rohnert Park?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public roadway defect, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's wise not to wait.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in Rohnert Park?
items.answer: Public-record collision counts show higher volumes along corridors like Rohnert Park Expressway, Redwood Drive, and Golf Course Drive, with more reports occurring on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply reported patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the accident. Any settlement or award would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it would not bar you from recovering altogether.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in typical personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specific facts of your case rather than a statutory ceiling.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you won't owe an attorney fee unless you recover compensation.
